subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Session Architecture: Shared LLM + Isolated Sessions + Public Knowledge Base

question: What session architecture should OpenClaw standardize on for isolated contexts, selected shared channel bindings, topic/session families, and shared durable memory?
rationale: Current main implements adjacent lifecycle primitives, but the remaining work changes product semantics, config contracts, privacy boundaries, migration behavior, and channel routing across several overlapping proposals.

options.title: Decompose one explicit architecture
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, choose the shared contracts, then split implementation into protocol/store, routing, UI, memory/security, docs, and migration slices.

options.title: Close umbrella in favor of narrower trackers
options.body: Move discussion to focused issues such as topic families, selected shared sessions, Google Chat group ingress, and UI lifecycle, accepting that no single issue tracks the full architecture.

options.title: Defer shared-memory layer
options.body: Land only isolated-session and UI lifecycle improvements for now while keeping public knowledge/RAG sharing out of core until the privacy model is approved.

recommendation.title: Decompose one explicit architecture
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella, choose the shared contracts, then split implementation into protocol/store, routing, UI, memory/security, docs, and migration slices.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest visible history across the current session lifecycle implementation and recent maintainer review context for this session architecture cluster.
